=== 3. OWNER VERDICT on the flagged fit-check scope (dispatch_worker_memory_max) ===
Reviewer flag: belt_user_work_slice_fit reads instance.dispatch_worker_memory_max; "confirm no build-sizing intent."
Trace: belt_user_work_slice_fit has EXACTLY two callers:
- roadmap_belt_actuate.dag:12595 belt_review_spawn -> requests instance.dispatch_worker_memory_max
- roadmap_belt_actuate.dag:12286 belt_audit_spawn   -> requests instance.dispatch_worker_memory_max
The units those spawns launch enforce MemoryMax = instance.dispatch_worker_memory_max:
- reviewer unit: dispatch_review_unit_command -> dispatch_review_unit_properties (dag/gunbc/roadmap/roadmap_dispatch_actuator.dag:1427)
- auditor unit:  dispatch_audit_unit_command (roadmap_dispatch_actuator.dag:1533) calls the SAME dispatch_review_unit_properties (line 1545) -> same MemoryMax
So BOTH fit checks request exactly the ceiling their own transient unit enforces, which is the DESIGN 3b reservation==enforced-cap identity. Neither sizes a compute BUILD.
compute_build_memory_ceiling is read ONLY by dag/gunbc/compute/host_capacity.dag:353 compute_memory_ceiling (the ComputeBuildPool appropriation via host_capacity_pool_seat_ceiling) — an orthogonal admission; it has ZERO readers in belt/roadmap. design_ruling.dag:634 states agents "should NOT get a build-sized allocation. Builds and tests go to remote/compute," which is exactly the split here.
VERDICT: NOT a defect; the checks correctly size the agent-session (reviewer/auditor transient), not a compute build. Changing either to compute_build_memory_ceiling would be WRONG: it would over-reserve a unit the kernel caps at dispatch_worker_memory_max and break the reservation==enforced-cap identity. NO CODE CHANGE made.
